pairs.why: A's orange stripe and trim give it the real cards' saturated multi-color accents and solid, well-built parts, while B's thin gold trim reads sleeker, glossier and more monochrome.
B is the orange-accented helmet with clearly built, chunky parts like the real cards; A's gold-trim version is glossier and plainer.
A has more functional detail (vents, buttons, orange rings), so it reads more like a real built object, like the preferred lesson drawings, though its house badge on the ear disc looks slightly odd.
B has the richer detail (vents, buttons, orange bands), like the real cards; A's gold-trim shell is smoother and glossier, closer to a statue.
